name: Abū al-Ḥasan ʿAlī ibn al-Mubārak al-Aḥmar
summary: Al-Kisāʾī's companion and the first to write down his teaching, tutor of the caliph al-Amīn, said by Thaʿlab to have known forty thousand lines of verse cited in grammar.
bio: Al-Aḥmar came to al-Kisāʾī as a youth and became his closest companion and the first to write down what he taught; al-Farrāʾ, who found him there 'with his beard just beginning to grow', later learned from him. He was tutor to al-Amīn, and in al-Kisāʾī's lifetime he was ranked above al-Farrāʾ.

Thaʿlab said he knew by heart forty thousand lines of verse cited as evidence in grammar, besides the odes and the rare words. Al-Zubaydī counts him in the third generation of the grammarians of Kufa. By Ibn al-Anbārī's account he died before al-Farrāʾ, in 206 or 207, and al-Farrāʾ said: 'Gone is the one who used to disagree with me in grammar.'
uncertain: Other biographers give 194/810 for his death; Ibn al-Anbārī has 206 or 207.

sources.title: Ibn al-Anbārī, Nuzhat al-alibbāʾ fī ṭabaqāt al-udabāʾ (Cairo 1294/1877), pp. 125–126
